what: ONE control run: N1's discrete problem - the SAME baseline mesh file, the SAME one-level Palace Model.Refinement.Boxes prescription, the SAME order, tolerances and eigenvalue target as the completed N1 - plus the ONE Solver.Linear override N2R used, MGMaxLevels: 1. It exists so that the refinement step N1R -> N2R has the same preconditioner strategy on both sides, and so that N1 vs N1R measures the solver-path effect on an identical discrete problem. It is NOT a new refinement level, NOT the prepared gmsh R2 experiment, and NOT a re-interpretation of N1.
approved_by: the repository owner, approving a single controlled rerun of N1 with MGMaxLevels: 1 after reviewing the N2R outcome
sequential: one run per invocation. This approval runs N1R ONLY and stops. Any other level, box, solver setting, R2 or a rerun of any completed run is a separate approval.

dry_runs_first.requirement: dry-run levels 2 and 3 and record measured DOF for both before running anything
dry_runs_first.note: both plain levels are inside the 250 000-DOF rule at order 1 and outside it at order 2, which is why this check is at order 1. R1 measures 80 762 DOF at order 1, 32.3 % of the rule and 818 DOF (1.0 %) above the plain level-2 baseline it is compared against.

constraints.external_or_additional_compute: none; one job on the standard GitHub-hosted runner
constraints.driver_refuses_above_budget: scripts/palace_order1_ladder.py measures DOF from the offline dry run and does not launch a level above the rule
constraints.port_refinement_is_read_from_this_record: every number comes from this file; no code change can introduce a refinement
constraints.distant_size_prescription: unchanged: h_far, the halo and the conductor/etch Distance field are the baseline's. The Box field returns h_far outside the padded box and is combined by Min, so it can only refine.

field_output.boundary_postprocessing: two interface-dielectric probes on the port face, Default and MA, unit thickness and unit permittivity
field_output.purpose: test the supported-but-unproven port-stiffness explanation of the energy-balance failures
field_output.committed: surface-Q.csv is committed with the record; the paraview/ tree is uploaded as an artifact only
field_output.carried_from: the N1 and N2 approvals, unchanged. Its 'purpose' field states the question N1 was approved to ask, which N1R re-asks on the identical problem; it is not a claim that this control run tests anything new.

rules_preserved_unchanged: the matching rule qmhp-cem.mode-matching/0.1.1 (two orderings plus the separation guard)
the magnitude comparison convention for participation
the frozen Delta|p| <= 1e-2 and Delta f <= 1e-4 criteria, reported and not gating
explicitly_out_of_scope: a third refinement level, which is a separate approval
the R2 gmsh mesh, still prepared and NOT approved
rerunning N2, N2R or the plain rungs
the Route A inversion on EM data
any change to the 250 000-DOF rule or the 45-minute cap
any change to the tolerances, the eigenvalue target, the mesh or the element order
a second control attempt or any other solver setting, each a separate approval
note: Committing this file on a palace/** branch starts the approved level. It is the approval record and the trigger at once, so a level cannot be started by an unrelated code change.

reruns.solve: COMPLETED; Palace ran and wrote its outputs, and the 173 MB field artifact uploaded
reruns.why_rerun: a defect in the reporting, not in the science: the driver rendered its report BEFORE writing the manifest and the record pointer, and the renderer raised KeyError on a result the convergence estimator is designed to return - the first tracked mode admitted no positive order of convergence. The record was therefore never manifested, uploaded or committed, and that solve's outputs were lost with the runner. The approved level is unchanged and is re-run.
reruns.fixed_by: summary.json and the record pointer are now written before any rendering; a render failure is captured into report.md and reported as a non-zero exit while the record is still manifested. The renderer handles every refusal the estimator can return, covered by a parametrised test over all six combinations including the one that failed.
reruns.note_for_the_rerun: attempt 1 told us something before it fell over: the fluxonium-like mode's frequency sequence over L1, L2, L3 admits NO positive order of convergence. That is a result, not a failure, and the rerun should reproduce it.

reruns.solve: NOT RUN - this is a record of what was fixed before spending the solve
reruns.why: the post-solve path had never executed with a port refinement. A prepare-only dry run of the full driver found render_report() raising KeyError('dof_measured'), because next_level_disposition returns the refinement branch for a refined run and the renderer assumed the level-3 shape. On the real run that would have cost the solve's report; the record would have survived, but only because the evidence-before-presentation fix was already in place.
also_fixed: earlier_rungs() excluded a refined record only by lexicographic accident; any label sorting before the plain record (e.g. one starting with a digit) would have put a different mesh into the convergence fit. Now excluded explicitly by payload.
the driver computed only the superseded fitted-kappa port_field_analysis; the derived diagnostic is now computed into the record alongside it.
the driver compared only against the level-1 reference; it now also compares against the plain rung at the same level, which is the comparison this run exists for.
TAGS was used in the new diagnostic without being imported, which would have raised NameError inside the post-solve path.

h_port_note: the owner wrote h_port = 0.003333 mm, which is the rounded form of h_gap(level 2)/2 = 0.006666666666666666/2. The exact double is used here because the mesh hash above is for that exact value; a truncated literal could build a different mesh and the hash gate would then correctly refuse to solve it.

what_this_run_answers.purpose: to put the same solver strategy on both sides of the N1 -> N2 refinement step, and to measure the solver-path effect directly on an identical discrete problem (N1 vs N1R).
what_this_run_answers.what_it_does_not_answer: nothing about the physics or the discretisation that N1 was not already approved to ask. The field_output block is N1's and N2's, carried unchanged.

comparisons.computed_by_this_run: original L2 -> N1R (baseline_record is the plain rung, as for N1)
comparisons.computed_offline_afterwards: N1R -> N2R through the driver's own compare_against_baseline with N1R as the baseline and N2R's committed record as the entry; and N1 vs N1R as a same-problem comparison under the same match_runs rule. scripts/controlled_sequence_comparison.py; output written beside the N1R candidate, never inside a results/ record.
comparisons.why_not_at_run_time: the driver compares a run only against a SHALLOWER baseline, and N2R is deeper than N1R; N2R's record is history and is not modified.

remaining_confounds: the refined region is a volume, not the port face

the green closure extends the refinement beyond the marked region: N1 measured it on this exact mesh and box - +4 541 DOF over the loaded mesh, of which 2 621 lie beyond the 221 marked tets (n1-nested-refinement-outcome.md sections 1 and 6) - and N1R must reproduce that count exactly
the marked tets average radius-ratio 0.2197 against the mesh's 0.3700, so element quality is a live alternative explanation
p_Default on the port face is unconverged at every level measured so far
two points cannot establish an order of convergence, and none is claimed

mechanism.what_refines: Palace, on the mesh it loads, via Model.Refinement.Boxes
mechanism.conforming: yes -- GeneralRefinement forces nonconforming=0 for 3-D simplex meshes (mesh.cpp:10565-10567)
mechanism.nested: yes -- ParMesh bisection inserts only edge midpoints; every baseline vertex survives (mesh.cpp:10834-10841)
mechanism.mesh_file: the baseline's, byte-identical. execute_level refuses with REFUSED-MESH-MISMATCH unless the mesh it builds hashes to baseline_mesh_sha256.
mechanism.propagates_outside_the_box: YES. Conformity is restored by a green-closure loop that bisects any element needing it, marked or not (pmesh.cpp:3467-3477), plus boundary elements (3568-3580). This is NOT a face-only or box-only change.
mechanism.invariant: w, l, L_s, kappa and Lc are unchanged. w and l come from the bounding box of the port attribute and midpoints cannot extend it; Lc is computed pre-refinement (main.cpp:311-313).

dof_rule.why_this_is_a_prediction_not_an_estimate: N1 ran this exact mesh and box; its probe read 84 485. N1R must reproduce that count, or the mesh is not N1's and the control is void.
dof_rule.how_it_is_enforced: the DOF probe, unchanged. It matches 'ND (p = 1): N' in Palace's 'Assembling system matrices' line, which prints the FINEST space once per run, before the multigrid hierarchy block. MGMaxLevels: 1 removes hierarchy lines the probe never matched; N2's log confirms the probe read exactly one value.

mesh_identity_check.euler: V - E + F - T = 1, so these are one consistent complex rather than four loose numbers. NECESSARY, not sufficient: the same characteristic holds for the baseline (13991-79944+130388-64434) and for N1 (14667-84485+138118-68299). What GUARANTEES the mesh is the hash gate on the mesh file plus the identical box prescription; these counts are the cross-check that the gate and the box did what they say.
mesh_identity_check.print_shape: with one mesh, geodata.cpp:394-400 prints a single un-prefixed 'Parallel Mesh Stats' block carrying the REFINED counts, as N2R did; N1 printed 'Coarse' and 'Refined'.

stop_conditions: Palace reports order-1 DOF above 250 000 -> the probe kills the container; REFUSED-DOF-BUDGET.
the built mesh does not hash to baseline_mesh_sha256 -> REFUSED-MESH-MISMATCH, nothing solved.
wall clock exceeds the unchanged 45-minute cap -> terminate and record TIMEOUT.
Palace exits non-zero, including on memory exhaustion -> record RUN_FAILED.
max backward error exceeds the unchanged 1e-6 -> record and stop.
the admitted set is not {m1, m2}, or matching against the plain L2 rung refuses -> record and stop.
any post-solve analysis raises -> the record is still written, manifested and committed.
completing N1R means STOP for review. A second control attempt, any other solver setting, or any further level is a separate approval.

solver_change.documented_as: configfile.hpp:776 - 'set to 1 to disable multigrid'. A supported setting.
solver_change.why: N2R's committed record compares it against N1, which ran a two-level V-cycle where N2R ran one level with the preconditioner applied directly. That step is not preconditioner-controlled and the record says so. N1R removes the difference: with it, L2 (1 level, unrefined), N1R (1 level) and N2R (1 level) form a refinement sequence with the same solver strategy at every point. The mechanism and its verification are unchanged from the N2R approval and are recorded in docs/coupled-candidate/n2-runtime-diagnosis.md and n2r-outcome.md.
solver_change.what_it_changes: one branch. The reserve at geodata.cpp:204 is skipped, so capacity() stays 1, :346 does not copy, and :350 runs the SAME GeneralRefinement(refs, -1) in place. multigrid.hpp:88 then builds a ONE-level hierarchy and ksp.cpp:202 applies the preconditioner directly.
what_it_does_not_change: the mesh file (the baseline's, hash-gated before launch) or the refined mesh it produces
the finite element order, the FE spaces or the assembled operators
Solver.Eigenmode N 6, Tol 1e-06, Target 0.5 GHz, Save 6
the materials, the lumped port, L_s, kappa, Lc and the boundary conditions

side_effect_paths_checked.RebalanceMesh: fires at geodata.cpp:353-355 only on this path, and is inert here: it returns 1.0 at Mpi::Size(comm)==1 (geodata.cpp:1445-1448) and its only preceding work is gated on save_adapt_mesh, default false (configfile.hpp:169). The run uses one MPI process.
side_effect_paths_checked.ReorientTetMesh: reachable at geodata.cpp:362 when mesh.size()==1, but gated on reorient_tet, default false (configfile.hpp:206) and not set.

solver_change.enforced_by_the_driver: an approval may override ONLY MGMaxLevels and MGUseMesh (scripts/palace_order1_ladder.py::_SOLVER_LINEAR_OVERRIDE_KEYS). Tol, MaxIts, Type and KSPType are refused before any solve is launched, so an approval cannot change what 'converged' means.

resource_expectation.no_runtime_is_predicted: N2R solved a LARGER problem, 103 411 DOF, on this configuration in 159.0 s, and N1R's operator is 18 % smaller. That is context. No runtime is predicted.
risks: the direct factorisation is slower than expected -> TIMEOUT at the unchanged cap
the direct factorisation exhausts runner memory -> RUN_FAILED
resource_expectation.either_is_the_result: recorded and reported as the outcome. The cap, the budget and the solver configuration are not changed to rescue it, and there is no second attempt under this approval.

n2_outcome_for_context.progress_when_killed: EPS restart 2 with 4 of 6 eigenvalues converged; N1 needed 3 restarts
n2_outcome_for_context.note: N2's timeout stands as recorded. N2R does not replace it and does not reinterpret it.

n2r_outcome_for_context.note: N2R stands as recorded. N1R does not modify or reinterpret it; the controlled comparison is computed offline from the two records.

sequence_records_note: deliberately empty. A one-level run's sequence IS its baseline comparison (original L2 -> N1R, in section 5c of the report); naming the plain rung here would add a one-step 'sequence' whose report banner says the step is 'not against a plain rung', which for N1R is exactly what it is. The solver-controlled sequence L2 -> N1R -> N2R is assembled offline from the records instead.
